topic_ko: 소비자 심리를 반영한 성난 외관의 자동차 디자인 트렌드
_note: 요지(논설문) FULL set. 유형마다 passage를 다르게 paraphrase. grammar/vocab/blank/implication의 밑줄·빈칸·함축 어구는 해당 passage 문장에 글자 그대로 존재. order/insert/irrelevant는 구조 재배열.

passage: Automakers have long understood that car buyers do not simply evaluate a vehicle for its mechanical performance.
People instinctively respond to the front of a car as if it were a human or animal face.
Recognizing this, designers deliberately craft front-end aesthetics to trigger specific emotional reactions.
Research confirms that the majority of drivers form their first impressions of a car through its headlights and grille.
By the early twenty-first century, this insight had driven a clear shift toward more aggressive, intimidating front profiles.
Analysts suggested that such menacing designs gave drivers a feeling of power and protection in increasingly crowded traffic.
A decade and a half later, strong sales figures showed no reversal of the trend.
In short, the angrier a car looks, the more confidently many consumers choose it.
choices: 성난 외관의 자동차 디자인은 소비자의 심리적 필요를 반영하며 인기를 끌고 있다.
자동차 제조사들은 차량 성능보다 연료 효율성 개선을 우선시하고 있다.
소비자들은 자동차를 구매할 때 주로 내부 편의 시설을 기준으로 판단한다.
자동차 디자인의 국제 표준화가 글로벌 판매 증가를 이끌고 있다.
운전자들은 교통 혼잡을 줄이기 위해 소형 차량을 선호하는 경향이 있다.
gist.explanation_ko: 자동차 제조사들이 소비자의 감정 심리를 반영하여 성난 외관의 차를 디자인하고 있고, 이것이 실제 판매 호조로 이어지고 있다는 것이 글의 요지. ①이 정답.
gist.distractor_ko: ②연료 효율, ③내부 편의시설, ④국제 표준화, ⑤소형차 선호는 모두 본문에 없는 내용이다.

passage: Car manufacturers are aware that consumers develop emotional connections to the fronts of vehicles.
This psychological insight shapes both design decisions and marketing campaigns in the automotive industry.
Experts in psychology and anthropology are consulted, and even brain-wave data from test groups is collected.
Studies suggest that the overwhelming majority of drivers recognize and evaluate a car by its face.
In the early twenty-first century, the dominant aesthetic direction moved toward fiercer, more threatening front designs.
One theory holds that these powerful-looking vehicles make drivers feel better protected amid ever-larger SUVs.
The trend has shown remarkable staying power, with aggressive styling continuing to drive strong sales years later.
Ultimately, automakers' exploitation of consumer psychology has made the angry car a commercial success.
choices: how fuel-efficiency regulations are reshaping automotive design worldwide
the role of consumer psychology in driving the trend toward aggressive car design
why safety certification standards differ across international car markets
the impact of digital advertising on automobile purchase decisions
how classic car aesthetics are making a comeback in modern showrooms
theme.explanation_ko: 소비자 심리(얼굴 인식·감정 반응)가 자동차의 공격적 디자인 트렌드를 이끌고 있다는 것이 글의 주제. ②가 정답.
theme.distractor_ko: ①연비 규제, ③안전 인증 기준, ④디지털 광고, ⑤클래식 미학의 귀환은 본문의 핵심 논점과 무관하다.

passage: People see faces everywhere ― and car fronts are no exception.
Automakers have turned this quirk of human perception into a core design strategy.
By consulting behavioral scientists and tracking neural responses, they craft front profiles that hit emotional targets.
Data shows that most drivers judge a car within seconds, based solely on its headlights and grille.
Beginning in the early 2000s, the industry deliberately pushed toward angrier, more aggressive looks.
The logic was straightforward: intimidating designs made buyers feel dominant and safe on increasingly dangerous roads.
And the market agreed ― sales of scowling, power-projecting vehicles climbed steadily through the 2010s.
The angry car is not a side effect of modern design; it is a calculated response to what consumers crave.
choices: Safety First: How Airbag Technology Changed the Car Industry
Behind the Scowl: Why Automakers Design Cars to Look Angry
The Rise of Electric Vehicles and Their Clean Aesthetic
Faces in the Machine: A History of Humanoid Robot Design
Bigger Is Better: Consumer Demand for Oversized SUVs
title.explanation_ko: 자동차 제조사들이 소비자의 심리를 이용하여 의도적으로 '성난 얼굴'의 차를 설계한다는 내용을 압축하는 ②가 제목으로 가장 적절하다.
title.distractor_ko: ①에어백, ③전기차, ④로봇 디자인, ⑤SUV 대형화는 글의 핵심 주제가 아니다.

passage: Car manufacturers know people form emotional attachments to automobile 'faces' and use the fact to guide their design and marketing efforts.
In today's hyper-competitive car market, designers are focusing on faces as part of a broader effort to design cars that appeal to buyers.
Automotive research shows that 70% of drivers identify and judge vehicles by the headlights and grille.
In the first years of the twenty-first century, the trend was toward angrier, scarier vehicles' faces.
The article hypothesized that these faces help drivers feel more safely in heavier traffic amidst more oversize SUVs.
Reflecting our tumultuous times, the 'scary look' shows no sign of slowing in the new millennium.
Buoyant sales of cars with styling which suggests power or bad temper seem to confirm that customers are happy with this look.
grammar.explanation_ko: ④ help + 목적어 + 동사원형(또는 형용사) 구문에서 feel 뒤에 오는 보어는 부사가 아닌 형용사여야 한다. 'feel more safely'는 틀리고 'feel safer'로 고쳐야 한다.
grammar.distractor_ko: ①주격 관계사절 that appeal to buyers, ②병렬 동사 identify and judge, ③비교급 angrier, scarier, ⑤분사구문 Reflecting은 모두 어법상 옳다.

passage: Car manufacturers know people form emotional attachments to automobile 'faces' and exploit the fact to guide their design and marketing efforts.

Reflecting our tumultuous times, the 'scary look' shows no sign of slowing in the new millennium.
Buoyant sales of cars with styling which suggests power or bad temper seem to confirm that customers are happy with this look.
vocab.explanation_ko: ④ 원문은 '가설을 세웠다(hypothesized)'인데, 아직 검증되지 않은 추론이므로 confirmed(확인했다)는 문맥에 맞지 않는다 → hypothesized로 고쳐야 한다.
vocab.distractor_ko: ①exploit(활용하다), ②appeal to(마음을 끌다), ③angrier, scarier(더 성나고 무서운), ⑤buoyant(활발한)는 모두 문맥에 적절하다.

passage: Car manufacturers know people form emotional attachments to automobile 'faces' and use the fact to guide their design and marketing efforts.
Designers consult psychologists and anthropologists, and even monitor brain-wave data from focus groups.
Research confirms that 70% of drivers identify and judge vehicles by the headlights and grille.
In the early twenty-first century, the dominant trend moved toward angrier, scarier vehicles' faces.

Reflecting the anxieties of our age, this 'scary look' continues to thrive.
In general, __________, the more buoyant the sales figures for that vehicle.
By 2017, an international automotive site confirmed that customers remained enthusiastic about power-projecting designs.
choices: the angrier and more aggressive a car looks
the smaller and lighter the vehicle
blank.explanation_ko: 빈칸 뒤에 '해당 차량의 판매 수치가 더 활발하다'고 했고, 전후 맥락은 성난 외관이 소비자에게 호소력을 가진다는 내용이다. '차가 더 성나고 공격적으로 보일수록(the angrier and more aggressive a car looks)' 판매가 더 좋다는 흐름이므로 ③이 정답.
blank.distractor_ko: ①연비, ②안전 등급, ④오래된 디자인, ⑤차체 소형화는 본문이 제시하는 '외관의 공격성'과 무관하다.

passage: Car manufacturers know people form emotional attachments to automobile 'faces' and use the fact to guide their design and marketing efforts.
Designers tap psychologists and anthropologists to craft car fronts that hit emotional targets in buyers.
Research shows that 70% of drivers identify and judge vehicles by the headlights and grille alone.
In the early twenty-first century, the trend moved decidedly toward angrier, scarier vehicles' faces.
Such faces were theorized to help drivers feel dominant and protected in ever-heavier traffic.
Reflecting our tumultuous times, the 'scary look' shows no sign of slowing in the new millennium.
Strong sales year after year seem to confirm that customers are content with — even hungry for — this scowling aesthetic.
The road, it seems, has become a stage where the car's face speaks louder than its engine.
implication.underlined: The road, it seems, has become a stage where the car's face speaks louder than its engine.
choices: a vehicle's visual appearance has come to matter more to buyers than its mechanical performance
roads are now considered more dangerous than they were in the previous century
car engines have grown quieter due to advances in noise-reduction technology
drivers use the road as a space to practice theatrical performances
automakers now invest more in road construction than in vehicle engineering
implication.explanation_ko: "도로는 자동차의 얼굴이 엔진보다 더 크게 말하는 무대가 됐다"는 표현은, 자동차의 시각적 외관(얼굴)이 기계적 성능(엔진)보다 구매자에게 더 중요하게 작용한다는 의미이다. ①이 정답.
implication.distractor_ko: ②도로 위험성, ③엔진 소음 감소 기술, ④연극 공연, ⑤도로 건설 투자는 모두 글의 핵심 비유와 무관하다.

order.given: Car manufacturers know people form emotional attachments to automobile 'faces' and use the fact to guide their design and marketing efforts.

blocks.A: The article hypothesized that these faces help drivers feel safer in heavier traffic amidst more oversize SUVs. Reflecting our tumultuous times, the 'scary look' shows no sign of slowing in the new millennium.
blocks.B: Automotive research shows '70% of drivers identify and judge vehicles by the headlights and grille.' In the first years of the twenty-first century, the trend was toward angrier, scarier vehicles' faces.
blocks.C: Designers are focusing on faces, tapping psychologists, anthropologists and other experts in human behavior, and even monitoring the brain waves of focus-group participants.

order.explanation_ko: 주어진 글(얼굴 애착 활용)에 이어 (C)에서 구체적 방법론(뇌파 모니터링 등)을 설명하고, (B)에서 연구 데이터(70%)와 트렌드('성난 얼굴')를 제시하며, (A)에서 그 이유(심리적 안전감)와 지속성(새 천년에도 둔화 없음)으로 마무리한다. (C)-(B)-(A).
order.distractor_ko: (B)의 '70% 데이터'는 (C)의 '얼굴 집중 이유'가 먼저 나온 뒤에 자연스럽고, (A)의 '이 얼굴들이 도움이 된다는 가설'은 (B)의 '성난 얼굴 트렌드' 이후에 온다.

insert.insert_sentence: Automotive research shows "70% of drivers identify and judge vehicles by the headlights and grille," the article reported.

insert.explanation_ko: 주어진 문장은 '운전자의 70%가 헤드라이트·그릴로 차를 판단한다'는 데이터로, ② 앞의 '디자이너들이 얼굴에 집중한다'는 방법론을 수치로 근거 지우고, ③ 뒤의 '성난 얼굴 트렌드'로 이어지는 흐름을 만든다. 따라서 ②가 정답.
insert.distractor_ko: ①의 앞 '얼굴 애착' 진술 직후는 아직 전문가 방법론 설명 전이고, ③④⑤는 이미 트렌드·가설·지속성으로 넘어간 뒤라 데이터 삽입 위치로 어색하다.

passage: Car manufacturers know people form emotional attachments to automobile 'faces' and use the fact to guide their design and marketing efforts.
Designers tap psychologists, anthropologists and even brain-wave monitoring to create car fronts with emotional impact.
Research shows 70% of drivers identify and judge vehicles by the headlights and grille.
In the early twenty-first century, the trend moved toward angrier, scarier vehicles' faces.
The article hypothesized that these faces help drivers feel safer in heavier traffic amidst more oversize SUVs.
Reflecting our tumultuous times, the 'scary look' shows no sign of slowing in the new millennium.

summary.summary_template: Car manufacturers deliberately design vehicles with __(A)__ front profiles because consumers psychologically associate such looks with safety and power, and __(B)__ sales data confirm that this strategy resonates with buyers.
summary.explanation_ko: 자동차 제조사는 소비자가 안전감·권력감을 느끼도록 (A)aggressive(공격적인) 앞면을 설계하고, 판매 데이터는 이 전략이 효과 있음을 (B)strong(강한/활발한) 수치로 뒷받침한다. ①이 정답.
summary.distractor_ko: (A)는 friendly(친근한)나 minimal(최소화된)이 아니라 aggressive, (B)는 declining(감소하는)이나 weak(약한)이 아닌 strong이어야 한다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 우리의 격동적인 시대를 반영하여, '무서운 외모'는 새 천년에도 둔화될 기미를 보이지 않는다.
writing.answer: Reflecting our tumultuous times, the 'scary look' shows no sign of slowing in the new millennium.
writing.explanation_ko: 분사구문 Reflecting our tumultuous times + 주절 the 'scary look' shows no sign of slowing + 장소 in the new millennium.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 자동차 제조사들은 사람들이 자동차 '얼굴'에 감정적 애착을 형성한다는 것을 알고 있으며, 이 사실을 자신들의 디자인과 마케팅 활동의 지침으로 활용한다.
writing.answer: Car manufacturers know people form emotional attachments to automobile 'faces' and use the fact to guide their design and marketing efforts.
writing.explanation_ko: 주어 Car manufacturers + 동사 know + 목적절(people form emotional attachments) + and use the fact to guide their design and marketing efforts.

writing.question: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 그 기사는 이러한 얼굴이 더 혼잡한 교통 속에서 더 대형화된 SUV들 사이에서 운전자들이 더 안전하다고 느끼도록 도와준다고 가설을 세웠다.
conditions: help + 목적어 + 동사원형 구문을 사용할 것
writing.answer: The article hypothesized that these faces help drivers feel safer in heavier traffic amidst more oversize SUVs.
writing.explanation_ko: hypothesize that + 주어절 / help drivers feel safer(help + O + 동사원형) / amidst more oversize SUVs.

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: "Buoyant sales of cars with styling which suggests power or bad temper seem to confirm that customers are happy with this look," an international automotive site reported in 2017.
writing.answer: "권력이나 나쁜 기질을 암시하는 스타일링의 자동차들의 활발한 판매는 고객들이 이 외모를 좋아한다는 것을 확인해 주는 듯하다"라고 한 국제 자동차 사이트가 2017년에 보도했다.
writing.explanation_ko: buoyant sales(활발한 판매) / styling which suggests power or bad temper(권력이나 나쁜 기질을 암시하는 스타일링) / seem to confirm that ~(~을 확인해 주는 듯하다).

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에 근거하여 쓰시오.
writing.summary: Car manufacturers (A)___________ consumer psychology by designing cars with aggressive front faces, and the continued strong sales of such vehicles (B)___________ that this approach is welcomed by buyers.
writing.explanation_ko: (A) 자동차 제조사들은 소비자 심리를 "활용한다(use)". (B) 강한 판매 수치가 전략의 효과를 "확인해 준다(confirm)".

writing.context: In today's hyper-competitive car market, designers are focusing on faces as part of a broader effort to design cars that appeal to buyers ― ___________ psychologists, anthropologists and other experts in human behavior, and even monitoring the brain waves of focus-group participants.
writing.explanation_ko: tapping은 '활용하여, 이용하여'의 뜻으로, 분사구문으로 '심리학자·인류학자 등을 이용하면서'를 나타낸다.
